plan.activation_condition: Observable during maintained moderate-to-high presynaptic_rate trains where facilitation elevates u above baseline for long enough that replenishment cannot be treated as having one constant time scale; weakest near very low rate or u approximately baseline_utilization.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, varying presynaptic_rate already changes sustained u and depletion. The same mechanism extends in holdout to stronger trains by predicting disproportionately slower refill at similar x, not just proportionally larger depletion.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when activity-dependent modulation of replenishment vanishes, so the effective recovery time becomes the constant recovery_time_constant independent of u or presynaptic_rate.
plan.promotion_reason: A transient depression of replenishment is a dynamical fatigue process with memory; existing x and u do not uniquely encode how long high use has persisted, so a dedicated state is needed to distinguish equal instantaneous x,u pairs reached after short versus prolonged trains.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes vesicle recovery proceeds with a fixed time constant regardless of recent presynaptic use, omitting use-dependent slowing of recruitment/refilling during sustained activity.
plan.baseline_assumption: Vesicle recovery and facilitation time scales remain constant.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Activity-dependent fatigue of the replenishment machinery or reserve-pool mobilization, causing recovery of available vesicles to slow during prolonged high release demand and relax back afterward.
plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: for observed x and u, dx_dt = (1-x)/recovery_time_constant - presynaptic_rate*u*x, so the recovery part is independent of activity history and has a single linear dependence on depletion depth. Proposed refinement: let sustained release load build a replenishment-fatigue state that slows recovery, changing the scored target mapping itself because dx_dt at the same x can differ depending on recent high-rate/high-u exposure. Distinguishing condition: vary presynaptic_rate across maintained trains while holding the initial conditions and parent parameters shared. Compare times when x is similarly depleted but one condition has experienced stronger sustained facilitation/use. The child predicts more negative dx_dt in the stronger-use condition because recovery is additionally slowed; the parent with one fixed recovery_time_constant cannot reproduce that history-dependent curvature and must assign the same recovery at matched x regardless of prior load. This is scientifically admissible under moderate-to-high rates where facilitation is activated and depletion persists; under weak stimulation the added effect may be too small to separate, which is a limitation rather than hidden evidence.

plan.promotion_reason: A finite-throughput/refractory occupancy effect has memory under sustained activation; existing states x, u, and replenishment_fatigue do not represent transient site unavailability, so one additional state is needed to generate rate-dependent compression without conflating it with facilitation or vesicle replenishment.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes every increment in mean presynaptic rate produces a proportional increment in effective release opportunities, even during dense maintained firing.
plan.baseline_assumption: The presynaptic spike train is represented by a constant mean rate, and that rate drives depletion as an ideal Poisson-like linear hazard with no finite release-site occupancy or refractory bottleneck.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Temporary release-site occupancy/refractoriness limits how many presynaptic events can effectively trigger vesicle release per unit time, causing saturation of depletion demand at high firing rates.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the ideal linear-use assumption in the target mapping rather than adding another unrelated fatigue branch. This implies that once those states are matched at moderate rate, the parent cannot also produce a pronounced high-rate compression of further depletion using one shared parameter set. The child instead introduces finite release-site throughput/refractoriness, yielding a concrete curvature change in dx_dt versus presynaptic_rate: approximately parent-like at low rate, but less negative than the parent at high sustained rate because effective event transmission saturates. This contrast is observable under the actual protocol because presynaptic_rate is a supplied fixed condition, x is the scored state, and sustained trains permit any added occupancy state to evolve from its initial condition into an active regime. The effect is scientifically admissible when firing is dense enough that inter-event spacing approaches the release-site reset timescale; at low rates the mechanism is weak and the parent remains a good approximation. This is a target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary-trajectory embellishment, because dx_dt itself acquires a new nonlinear dependence on supplied presynaptic_rate through the effective depletion factor.

plan.baseline_assumption: Release-dependent depletion of the available vesicle pool is linear in the available-resource fraction x.
plan.scientific_mechanism: State-dependent release competence within the readily releasable pool: when the pool is nearly depleted, the remaining vesicles are less effectively release-ready on average, so effective depletion grows sublinearly with x rather than strictly linearly.

A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot reproduce this changed curvature across both regimes, because those parameters only rescale recovery and the overall linear depletion prefactor, not the shape of depletion versus x. plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes facilitation multiplies depletion with fixed efficacy regardless of the current fatigue state of vesicle replenishment, making depletion a separable product of facilitation and fatigue effects.
plan.baseline_assumption: Release-dependent depletion is modulated by facilitation and replenishment fatigue through independent multiplicative factors only; fatigue slows recovery but does not reshape how facilitation translates into resource consumption.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Under sustained use, residual-calcium-driven facilitation can become less effective at increasing actual vesicle consumption when replenishment/mobilization is fatigued, because extra release drive cannot be converted into proportionally more effective depletion once supply-side readiness is stressed.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the assumption of separable depletion gain. In the parent, varying u at fixed presynaptic_rate, x, and release_site_occupancy changes dx_dt through a single multiplicative factor, while replenishment_fatigue only slows the recovery branch. Thus the parent predicts the same facilitation-to-depletion gain shape early and late in a train once x is matched, apart from overall recovery offset. A scientifically plausible refinement is that high replenishment_fatigue reduces how strongly facilitation can convert presynaptic activity into actual vesicle loss, because the supply side becomes the bottleneck. The observable contrast is obtained by varying time within a maintained moderate-to-high-rate train while holding presynaptic_rate fixed and comparing epochs with low versus elevated replenishment_fatigue: the child predicts diminished marginal effect of u on dx_dt in the fatigued epoch, whereas the parent with one shared parameter set preserves a fixed separable u gain in the depletion term. This is admissible because replenishment_fatigue is already a modeled state that can enter a moderate range under sustained drive. The effect is limited when trains are too weak or short to build fatigue, in which case the child should reduce toward the parent.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when presynaptic_rate is high enough and stimulation long enough that replenishment_fatigue reaches moderate values while x and u remain nonzero; weak or negligible near replenishment_fatigue ≈ 0.

plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the extra fatigue dependence of depletion efficacy vanishes, so fatigue again enters dx_dt only through the shared 1/(1 + replenishment_fatigue) factor.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes replenishment fatigue attenuates vesicle recovery and vesicle consumption with the same simple multiplicative factor, which is likely too rigid once supply-side stress specifically limits conversion of facilitation drive into actual depletion.
plan.baseline_assumption: Replenishment fatigue acts as a single shared divisor on both recovery and depletion fluxes with identical dependence.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Under sustained use, fatigued mobilization/repriming reduces how effectively elevated facilitation and presynaptic drive can recruit releasable vesicles into actual consumption, producing an extra nonlinear saturation of depletion with fatigue beyond the recovery slowdown already present.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the fatigue coupling in the scored dx_dt itself, not merely an auxiliary equation. In the parent, if x, u, release_site_occupancy, and presynaptic_rate are held fixed, increasing replenishment_fatigue changes dx_dt through one shared reciprocal factor applied symmetrically to recovery and depletion. That imposes a specific curvature: both positive recovery and negative depletion weaken in lockstep as fatigue rises. Scientifically, however, late in a maintained high-rate train the supply side can become so stressed that extra facilitation no longer converts into proportionally more vesicle consumption, even though depleted pools still recover slowly. Thus the child should let depletion efficacy bend downward more strongly with replenishment_fatigue than recovery does. The observable contrast is obtained by varying sustained-use regime through presynaptic_rate and elapsed time while holding the model form and initial conditions fixed: early in the train, when replenishment_fatigue is near zero, parent and child agree closely; later, after fatigue accumulates to moderate levels, the child predicts dx_dt that is less negative than the parent at comparable u and release drive because depletion saturates more strongly. This is admissible under the current observation protocol because replenishment_fatigue is an existing observed state trajectory, so the changed target mapping is directly testable. A single refit of existing parent parameters cannot fully absorb this across both low- and moderate-fatigue conditions because the parent is constrained to one common fatigue divisor shared by recovery and depletion; changing that divisor's coefficient would move both fluxes together rather than selectively altering the curvature of the depletion branch.

response_change.parent_relation: The depletion term scales with facilitation and available resource as presynaptic_rate*(1 - release_site_occupancy)*u*x**2 divided by a fatigue factor, so for fixed observed u, x, and release_site_occupancy the target depends on replenishment_fatigue only through a simple reciprocal attenuation shared by both recovery and depletion.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that replenishment fatigue only rescales both fluxes equally by allowing depletion efficacy itself to saturate more strongly with fatigue than recovery does, creating a nonlinear bending of dx_dt versus replenishment_fatigue at fixed presynaptic_rate, u, x, and release_site_occupancy.
response_change.observable_effect: During sustained high-rate conditions that build appreciable replenishment_fatigue, the child predicts a stronger flattening or rollover of activity-driven depletion than the parent, so late-train dx_dt becomes less negative than expected from the parent's single reciprocal fatigue scaling even when u remains elevated.

diagnostic_groups.name: effective_release_drive
diagnostic_groups.role: Instantaneous event-weighted release demand on the available pool

diagnostic_groups.name: fatigue_load
diagnostic_groups.role: Current level of supply-side stress accumulated under sustained use

diagnostic_groups.name: depletion_flux_parent
diagnostic_groups.role: Parent effective depletion term to compare against late-train deviations

contract.activation_condition: Observable when presynaptic_rate is high enough and stimulation long enough that replenishment_fatigue reaches moderate values while x and u remain nonzero; weak or negligible near replenishment_fatigue ≈ 0.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, early versus late portions of the same maintained-rate episode already vary replenishment_fatigue; in holdout, stronger rates or longer trains extend the same contrast by pushing farther into the fatigued regime.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the extra fatigue dependence of depletion efficacy vanishes, so fatigue again enters dx_dt only through the shared 1/(1 + replenishment_fatigue) factor.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Under sustained use, fatigued mobilization/repriming reduces how effectively elevated facilitation and presynaptic drive can recruit releasable vesicles into actual consumption, producing an extra nonlinear saturation of depletion with fatigue beyond the recovery slowdown already present.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the added fatigue-dependent modulation selectively bends the depletion branch while leaving the recovery branch on its original fatigue law, changing the target curvature with respect to replenishment_fatigue rather than merely rescaling the whole RHS.
contract.assumption_before: Replenishment fatigue acts as a single shared divisor on both recovery and depletion fluxes with identical dependence.
contract.assumption_after: Replenishment fatigue still slows recovery as before, but it also separately and multiplicatively saturates depletion efficacy so facilitation-driven consumption weakens more strongly at higher fatigue.
contract.parent_reduction: When baseline_utilization*replenishment_fatigue is negligible, the extra modulation tends to 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
contract.observable_signature: At fixed observed x, u, release_site_occupancy, and presynaptic_rate, the parent gives dx_dt versus replenishment_fatigue from one shared reciprocal attenuation of both terms, whereas the child introduces extra downward bending only in the depletion branch. Thus early low-fatigue samples remain close to the parent, but late moderate-fatigue samples show dx_dt less negative than the parent predicts because depletion saturates more strongly than recovery.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce this contrast across low- and moderate-fatigue conditions because the parent structurally forces recovery and depletion to move together under the same factor 1/(1 + replenishment_fatigue). Retuning recovery_time_constant, presynaptic_rate, or baseline_utilization only rescales amplitudes or auxiliary trajectories, but cannot create selective fatigue curvature in the scored depletion contribution while preserving the low-fatigue behavior with one shared parameter set.
